dayLines: 💛 You hold Dispatcher's headset. Breathe. The shaking eases. (−6 trauma)
📖 LEARNED: Old World Caches (Level 1). You know where people hid things: under floorboards, in hollow trees, behind loose bricks.
You've learned Old World Caches — it carries Eagle Eye.

Travel 2 tiles to trail edge.
— An old trail —
The trail splits around a boulder and rejoins — the world's oldest traffic decision. You follow the deeper-worn side.
You see smoke on the horizon. Stonebridge — 8 people, 25 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 8 plants — 8 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
You catch fragments by the fire — Violet telling Ruby about you. Half of it's true anymore. You're not sure which half.
You catch fragments by the fire — Ruby telling Tamika about themself. Someone's added a flourish that wasn't there this morning.

Travel 1 tile to trail edge.
— An old trail —
The trail is worn smooth as an old coin. Deer, probably. Probably.
Stonebridge's clearing. Voices, a cookfire, somebody else's home. You're a guest here — act like it.

Travel 2 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Fallen trunks lie like sleeping animals, furred with moss. The ground gives underfoot — centuries of leaf-mold.
Movement — a black bear, powerful and intelligent-eyed.
👁 It's not scared — it's DECIDING. Two hundred pounds of deciding. Give it the exit, never the corner; noise and bigness buy you the day.

You see smoke on the horizon. The Red Table — 3 people, 25 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 6 plants — 6 new to you. They look lean — hungry, even. Food would talk here. They've been here the whole time.

Travel 1 tile to creek.
— Moving water —
The water is cold enough to hurt your teeth. Downstream the creek bends out of sight, and you want to follow it. That's the problem with creeks.

You see smoke on the horizon. Emberhold — 6 people, 25 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 9 plants — 8 new to you. They look lean — hungry, even. Food would talk here. They've been here the whole time.
The creek runs fast here — no crossing without a bridge or a swim.
